references.text: The clay pot in which the sin offering was boiled must be broken. This illustrates the same principle that clay vessels that have come into contact with holy or unclean things must be destroyed.
Continues the theme of uncleanness spreading to objects, where ovens and pots must be broken when they become unclean.
Parallel to the destruction of unclean things—here a house with leprosy is torn down, just as clay vessels must be broken.
Clay vessels touched by a man with a discharge must be broken, while wooden vessels are to be rinsed. This shows the difference between clay and other materials.
Open vessels without lids become unclean through contact with a dead body, extending the principle of uncleanness transferred to vessels.
Rules for cleansing objects after war, where some materials are purified with fire and others with water, in contrast to clay vessels which must be destroyed.
